races.title: State Senate, District 36
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Eddie Settle
cands.bio: Republican state senator for District 36 since January 2023. Wilkes County native and owner of Nu-Line Printing and Settle Cattle Company. Elected to the Wilkes County Board of Commissioners in 2012, where he served as chairman and vice chairman. Lives in Elkin.
cands.gaps: We found no documented stances from Settle on data centers, development, or growth and land conservation. We found no verified record of his actions on foreign or investor land ownership, immigration or H-1B, school choice or teacher pay, policing, or a clean-money pledge. Ballotpedia's list of bills he sponsored did not load in the page we read, so we could not review his sponsored legislation. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys, and Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him in 2022, 2024 or 2026. His campaign site is an older version that still refers to the Biden administration and to his county commissioner service as current. Claims there about his county votes could not be checked against county records. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties or birth date; Wikipedia gives only 1959 or 1960.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia says he was born in Wilkes County, and his campaign site calls him a Wilkes County native who graduated from East Wilkes High School in 1978 and has run local businesses there since 1979.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: State senator since 2023; Wilkes County commissioner since 2012, including time as chairman and vice chairman; owner of Nu-Line Printing (bought 1994) and Settle Cattle Company (founded 1990).
qual.why: Prior legislative service plus nearly a decade of local elected office, where county budgets are set, and decades as a business owner. A committee chair role was not counted toward the score.
qual.label: Prior legislative service plus nearly a decade of local elected office, where county budgets are set, and decades as a business owner. A committee chair role was not counted toward the score.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: His campaign site says he opposes tax increases, will never support one, and favors cutting unnecessary spending. It also says he never voted to raise taxes as a county commissioner and voted to lower them in 2016 (a self-reported claim). It does not mention homestead or primary-residence property taxes specifically.

pro-life.evidence: His campaign site says he is pro-life and that, as chairman of the Wilkes County commissioners, he brought to a vote a resolution designating the county a haven for the unborn, which he says passed unanimously (a self-reported claim).

second-amendment.evidence: His campaign site says he is an NRA member and will keep fighting for Second Amendment rights at the state level. It names no specific bills or policies.

prio.label: Matches 3 of 3 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 3 only promised

roots.summary: Ballotpedia says he was born in Wilkes County, and his campaign site calls him a Wilkes County native who graduated from East Wilkes High School in 1978 and has run local businesses there since 1979.

cands.name: Trevor Cole Hardwick
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for North Carolina State Senate District 36 in 2026. He advanced without a primary and lost the general election to incumbent Republican Eddie Settle. The sources available give no information on his occupation or any prior offices.

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia as receiving a voter guide recommendation from the Sway voting group "Reject AIPAC from City Council to Congress" (Vote for Peace).
Listed by Ballotpedia as receiving a voter guide recommendation from the Sway voting group "Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy" (Tevin (Momala) Davis).

cands.gaps: We could not find where Trevor Hardwick was born or raised, or when he moved to North Carolina. We found no information on his jobs, education or any offices he has held. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, and we found no campaign website or interviews, so his stated positions on the issues are unknown. We found no record of actions he has taken on any policy issue, and no documented stance on data centers or development. We found no news coverage of controversies.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: No occupation, career or prior elected office is documented in the available sources.
qual.why: His background could not be found, so no score is given.
qual.label: Background not found: unknown, not unqualified
